sources.citation: 符昌忠 Fu Changzhong. 2019. 那斗语动词的体范畴 [The aspect category of verbs in Nadou]. 民族语文 Minzu Yuwen 2019(1): 66-74.
sources.note: Verb-aspect morphology only, with tone-numbered transcriptions; scanned a full-text search for stress/accent finds no 重音/轻声/轻读/轻音. Useful for identity (Nadou = 来话, 2 villages, 3,380 speakers) and for the bibliography line 符昌忠《那斗语概况》《民族语文》2011年第3期.

sources.citation: Norquest, Peter K. 2007. A Phonological Reconstruction of Proto-Hlai. PhD dissertation, University of Arizona. 617 pp. hdl:10150/194203 (Glottolog 683655 lists it as 'A phonological system of Proto-Hlai').
sources.note: Historical-comparative only. Cunhua and Nadouhua tone/register tables (ex.17 p.76; ex.32 p.165: Cun A 35/13, B 21, C 42/13, D 33/13; Nadou A 11/21ʔ, B 25, C 42, D 21ʔ). All 18 occurrences of 'stress' concern reconstructed Pre-Hlai/Proto-Hlai iambic sesquisyllables (p.250: 'Disyllabic words were certainly iambic..'; pp.288-289 stress-to-weight hypothesis rejected; pp.317-323). No synchronic statement about word stress in Cunhua or Nadouhua anywhere.

sources.note: Historical phonology of Cun's Chinese-sourced vs Hlai-sourced vocabulary - coronal-initial chain shift *t>ɗ, *s>tθ, loan-phoneme strata; argues Chinese-sourced words are inherited and Hlai-sourced words borrowed after migration. The abstract does not mention tones; a 32-page correspondence study of Cun strata will almost certainly use tone-category correspondences as stratum diagnostics, but this was not seen.

sources.note: Norquest 2007 (ch. 1): 'Fu (1983) presented a short wordlist of Cunhua lexical items, the number of which was doubled in the follow-up publication of Ouyang & Fu (1988). So: a 10-page Minzu Yuwen article combining an enlarged Cunhua wordlist with a discussion of Cun's genetic classification; whether it tabulates tone categories/values was not seen.
